Let me tell you of an observation I made in Santiago, Chile.

I am a dog person. I have always kept dogs. I understand them, or so I thought. But when you are a master and a dog, there is a 1:1 relationship, you are the boss, you provide the food and water and back scratchies, and the dog obeys to the limits of his intelligence and mood.

I was lost in thought, walking through the central park in Santiago. I won't go into the Stephen King details, but the bold moments showed me couples relaxing, basking in love, every grassy knoll spotted with another potential bond. The busker and hustle of the streets didn't exist here. The birds sang, and they shit somewhere else.

I walked anti-clockwise around the park, relaxed, unthinking. As I made my way back to the highway on the northeast end of the park [as far as I knew] I saw the most satisfied and comfortable stray dog I have ever seen.

Having traveled in South America extensively, I was used to seeing strays. They had their own civilization, their gullies and sewers and shade bushes separate from us. In Moscow and London they and their Cat antithesis ride the damn metro. But this dog, this world was his.

And as I walked by, I saw another dog - lean and mean, but not wise. He walked by and the Fourth of July sprawling the Alpha dog of the park has been enjoying was over. Fireworks were on.

The Alpha dog ran over to attack him, this new dog was in the wrong place. Immediately and subsequently a half dozen other dogs ran to the scene - to nip and bite at the new dog who, individually, they wouldn't have approached.
